text: The Chemical Industry Medal is an annual award presented by the Society of Chemical Industry America (SCI America) to an industrial chemist. First awarded in 1933, it replaced the Grasselli Medal. Initially, the medal was given to "a person making a valuable application of chemical research to industry, with primary consideration given to applications in the public interest." By 1945, the criteria shifted to recognize "a person who ... has rendered conspicuous service to applied chemistry." More recently, the award has been given "for contributions toward the growth of the chemical industry."
